deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 23 is a continuous prose page of lecture notes on ancient Jewish history, continuing from folio 22 (David, Solomon) and running into folio 24 (the divided kingdoms, the prophets, the Messiah idea). The handwriting looks like a student's notebook (a course on ancient or universal history) rather than a Gauss working page. This is consistent with the bundle being a miscellany. Content, in order:

(1) Solomon's administration. The kingdom was divided into 12 districts (the notes say 'Stämme', tribes), each under a governor. Each district had to supply all the king's needs for one month of the year.

(2) Solomon greatly increased the prosperity of the land, partly through trade and partly through his own efforts.

(3) Solomon carried out the building of the Temple. Otherwise he had nothing of the warlike spirit of David.

(4) Solomon had to contend with rebels who wanted to push him from the throne and take it themselves.

(5) Solomon died in 975 [B.C.] and was to be succeeded by his eldest son Rehoboam. Jeroboam was one of the rebels and had fled to Egypt.

(6) Ten tribes fell away from Rehoboam because he threatened to lay even heavier burdens on them than Solomon had. As a result his kingdom consisted only of the two tribes Judah and Benjamin.

(7) New section heading: 'b. Der jüdische Staat als getrenntes Reich, 975 – 588'. Subheading: 'a) allgemeine Bemerkungen'.

(8) Point I: such a division could bring no good fortune to the Jews. Between the two kingdoms there was an eternal, deadly hatred, and one king raged against the other. The numbering continues with II–V on folio 24.

The dates 975 (division of the kingdom) and 588 (fall of Jerusalem) follow the conventional chronology of early-19th-century German history textbooks, e.g. the Heeren school. The section therefore serves no mathematical problem; there are no derivations to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors to assess.

Historically, the dates 975 BC (division) and 588 BC (fall of Jerusalem) are the traditional early-19th-century chronology. Modern chronology gives roughly 931/922 BC for the division and 587/586 BC for the destruction of Jerusalem. These reflect the period's conventions and are not slips by the writer.
Calling Solomon's 12 administrative districts 'Stämme' (tribes) is a simplification. 1 Kings 4 describes 12 prefectures that did not coincide with the tribal boundaries.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics at all. It is routine historical lecture material, likely in a student's or copyist's hand rather than Gauss's own, and of no significance for the history of mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The span of the 'getrenntes Reich' section heading (975 to 588 BC) is 387 years; this is the only arithmetic implicit on the page.
Twelve districts each supplying one month cover the full 12-month year, consistent with the described provisioning system.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the machine reading 'Ausserordentlich[?] vermehrte er' is plausible, but the image may read 'Außerordentlich erhöhte er'. The verb is uncertain.
Line 5: 'Salomo' is underlined in the original as a name heading. 'führte ... aus' fits the image.

Line 7: the line appears to begin with 'Geist.' completing the previous sentence ('nichts von dem kriegerischen Geist David[s]'). The machine transcription drops this word; read 'Geist. Salomo hatte mit Rebellen zu kämpfen'.
Lines 11–12: the doubled 'nach[?] nach Aegypten' is a transcription artifact. The image shows a struck-through or overwritten word at the line end, then 'nach Aegypten flüchten'.
Lines 14–15: 'Er dachte[?] sein Reich nur ... bestand[?]' is better read as 'So daß sein Reich nur aus den beiden Stämmen Juda und Benjamin bestand.'
Section point numbering: the first remark is numbered 'I.' (Roman numeral, matching II.–V. on folio 24), not '1.'.
Last line: likely 'tödlicher Haß, der König wüthete gegen den andern' (or 'ein König wüthete an andern'); the middle word remains uncertain.
